transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE - intro), Marcus (CISO, Ridgeway), Priya (Head of Platform), Luis (Legal), Katie (Infra)

--- Auto summary (generated) ---
Redwood walked through region pinning options, subprocessor disclosure timeline, and KMS key separation approach for EU-only processing. Customer asked for explicit guarantees around cross-border fallbacks and audit log export mechanisms.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jordan from Redwood, Elena and Ravi on the tech side. Marcus?
[00:08] Marcus: Hey, Marcus here, CISO at Ridgeway. Priya and Luis also on from our side.
[00:14] Jordan: Awesome. We flagged this as a security review — mostly around data residency, region routing, and subprocessors. Elena will run the tech deep-dive.
[00:24] Elena: Hi team, quick agenda: region pinning options (hosted routing vs dedicated), subprocessor onboarding and disclosure cadence, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), and audit log exports/retention. Also Q&A.
[00:33] Priya: That sounds good. Our main constraint: EU tenant data cannot leave EU control plane unless we have explicit consent and audit trail. We also want RBAC and SSO alignment with our IdP.
[00:44] Katie: For infra, the ask is: can we force EU-only routing for specific tenants and ensure no fallback to US? And what happens during capacity spikes?
[00:52] Elena: Good Q. Short answer: we support region affinity policies and strong region pinning at the routing layer. We can configure a per-tenant policy that prefers EU endpoints and denies cross-border fallback for the duration of the pin. For capacity spikes we offer two patterns: reserve Dedicated capacity in EU (Redwood Dedicated) or a controlled cross-border failover with encryption-in-transit plus audit flagging.
[01:14] Marcus: We want to avoid any automatic cross-border failover — that kills our compliance posture. Is dedicated capacity the only way to guarantee zero egress?
[01:25] Ravi: If you need strict no-egress, Dedicated or Private deployment inside your VPC is the only way to guarantee physical data locality. Hosted can be configured for affinity but has operational fallbacks unless you select a strict policy and reserve capacity.
[01:39] Marcus: Understood. What about KMS? We need customer-managed keys with separate envelope keys per region, ideally kept in our EU KMS.
[01:50] Elena: We support CMK integration — you can bring keys from your KMS (Azure Key Vault or Google Cloud KMS). For EU-only routing + CMK, keys can be provisioned in the EU region and Redwood will never persist plaintext outside the region. There are some caveats around metadata and model cache keys that we'll document.
[02:10] Priya: Caveats — can you expand? Metadata is the riskiest piece for us.
[02:15] Elena: Sure. Currently, metadata like routing logs and index pointers are stored in the control plane. For Private deployments we can localize the control plane or provide a filtered telemetry export. For hosted customers we keep metadata in our control plane but can limit PII and provide an audit trail on access.
[02:33] Marcus: Is the control plane the same as the one that might be in the US? We need assurances it's EU for EU tenants.
[02:39] Elena: For strict requirements we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with region-isolated control plane. Hosted EU region has a control plane region but some backend services and subprocessor calls (billing, metrics) may touch other regions — we'll enumerate those subprocessors in the inventory.
[02:55] Luis: Speaking of subprocessors, we need the list and onboarding cadence. Our procurement policy requires 30 days notice and subprocessors to be SOC 2 or ISO certified.
[03:06] Jordan: Absolutely — we have a living subprocessor CSV and SOC 2 snapshot. I'll put that in the folder. Our standard cadence is 30 days notice for material changes and an annual full inventory.
[03:18] Katie: What about ephemeral caching and KV cache — are those ever replicated cross-border? We have session affinity per tenant.
[03:25] Elena: KV cache is region-local by design for pinned tenants. There's a subtlety: prefix caching at the CDN or routing layer may be global; we'll ensure tenant-specific caches remain EU-local when pinning is enabled. There have been transcription/labeling quirks in some docs where KV became 'K V cache' so sorry if past docs were confusing.
[03:44] Marcus: Good to know. Another ask: audit logs. We need write-once logs, exportable to our SIEM with guaranteed retention for 7 years. Is that supported?
[03:54] Elena: We can stream audit logs to customer-owned GCS/S3 endpoints or to an on-prem collector via a secure forwarder. Retention is configurable; for hosted we provide standard retention, and long-tail archival can be exported to your bucket. Write-once semantics depend on customer storage settings — we recommend object-lock on your side.
[04:13] Marcus: How about proof — can you provide a sample log schema and proof of delivery?
[04:18] Jordan: We'll attach the log schema and a sample export flow. We also have a signed delivery confirmation for exports if needed; Elena will add the export examples to the runbook.
[04:27] Luis: Related legal question — do you support data subject requests for EU residents and how do you assert data lineage when data has been processed by model caches?
[04:36] Elena: We track lineage per request ID and cache prefix. For EU-resident tenants with pinning enabled, we can correlate request IDs and return artifacts or delete cache entries upon DSAR. There are some limits on model training caches — we don't use customer data to train public models, and we document that in the DPA.
[04:53] Priya: We're big on RBAC and SSO. How granular are the roles and can we map to our IdP groups?
[04:59] Ravi: We support SAML/SSO + SCIM provisioning. RBAC roles can be fine-grained: tenant admin, read-only ops, billing view, API-only keys. You can also configure restrictions so that some roles cannot perform cross-border exports.
[05:17] Marcus: Good. Can we audit user-level actions in the console? Need to know who triggered a model switch or a fallback.
[05:24] Elena: Yes — every route change, rollout, and canary action is logged with user ID and timestamp. Those logs can be included in the audit stream.
[05:31] Priya: On the routing side, can we do per-model routing? E.g., use a smaller quantized variant for EU and a higher-capacity model in US? We want consistent semantics but different SLAs per region.
[05:44] Elena: Yes — policies can target routes by model and region. You can pin model version per tenant and also have automatic fallback to a quality-limited variant within the same region. Cross-region variant substitution requires explicit opt-in.
[05:59] Katie: During a sudden EU capacity surge, if we have no Dedicated reserve, what are our options? We need an SLO for availability.
[06:07] Ravi: Options: increase reserved capacity in EU (preferred), configure conservative queueing with backpressure and notify on overload, or allow controlled cross-border fallback with encryption + audit. The SLOs depend on the committed capacity SKU.
[06:23] Marcus: We want to avoid fallback. Cost is secondary to compliance. Give us pricing for Dedicated EU slices.
[06:30] Jordan: We'll send the Dedicated pricing by slice size and throughput. Also, for pilots we can provide a temporary credit for capacity so you can test EU-only routing.
[06:38] Priya: On subprocessors: if a subprocessor adds a new region we need automatic notification. Is that covered in your policy?
[06:46] Jordan: Yes — material changes require 30-day notice and we publish a change log. For emergency security patches, we have a shorter notification window but we will escalate via the designated contacts.
[06:58] Luis: Can we get a copy of your Data Processing Addendum with the EU SCCs and any vendor subprocessor obligations?
[07:05] Jordan: Yes — we'll share the DPA with SCC annex and redline suggestions. We'll also share contact for our legal team.
[07:12] Marcus: One more technical nit: where are your model weights stored? Could they be served from a centralized US blob that still results in EU inference?
[07:20] Elena: Model weights are cached on serving nodes per region. For hosted small models we sometimes reference a central object store for cold-start weights — we can ensure that for EU-pinned tenants the weights are cached in EU nodes; persistent storage of weights in EU can be arranged for Dedicated/private deployments. We'll call this out in the runbook.
[07:40] Priya: Outstanding question: KMS key rotation. If we rotate in our EU KMS, what is the expected downtime or re-encryption window?
[07:48] Elena: Rotation is seamless for envelope keys — we rotate the wrapping key and new tokens use the new key. For some cached tokens there can be a short window where we rewrap; the system retries and you'll see transient errors for < 2 minutes in most cases. We'll add best practices to the guide.
[08:04] Marcus: Can Redwood's auditors provide evidence of SOC 2 controls around key management?
[08:10] Jordan: Our SOC 2 snapshot includes KMS control descriptions. We can provide the report under NDA.
[08:15] Luis: We need to see the SOC2 and ISO cert copies. Also, do you align to any cloud provider's subprocessors? For example, if you run on GCP EU region, do you rely on any third-party monitoring vendor?
[08:27] Elena: We use a small set of monitoring subprocessors; we'll include those in the subprocessor spreadsheet. Most of them are SOC 2 compliant. For Hosted EU we rely on cloud provider networking but we can disclose specifics per deployment.
[08:41] Priya: Operational question: how fast can you onboard a new EU region for us if we sign agreement? We want a 2-week pilot spin-up.
[08:48] Ravi: For a basic EU pilot with small capacity, we can spin up in ~2 weeks if we have the legal and infra access in parallel. For Dedicated reserved capacity and KMS integration it's closer to 4-6 weeks.
[09:01] Marcus: Let's talk about audit log retention again — can you prove chain of custody if a support engineer accesses data for debugging? Who signs off?
[09:10] Elena: Access to tenant data by Redwood engineers requires a documented justification, a ticket, and RBAC approvals. Those actions are logged with ticket ID and can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include the ticket-workflow in the runbook.
[09:24] Jordan: Quick micro-recap: Jordan will send subprocessors and SOC2; Elena will send runbook sections on region pinning, KMS patterns, and audit export; Ravi will outline pilot timeline.
[09:36] Priya: Sounds good. One more thing: network egress costs — we're curious about any billing implications if we opt for cross-region replication for DR.
[09:45] Jordan: We'll include estimated egress and data transfer cost models in the pricing spreadsheet.
[09:51] Katie: Operational readiness: who will be our Redwood point of contact during the pilot? We want an SE and an escalation AE.
[09:58] Jordan: I'll be the primary AE contact, Elena will be SE. We'll add a dedicated Slack channel and Pager for production issues if we move to Dedicated.
[10:07] Marcus: Okay if we step through a hypothetical — tenant A is EU-only, spikes to 3x capacity, no Dedicated. What is the path of events?
[10:16] Elena: The routing layer will attempt queueing and throttling, then notify you; if you allowed cross-border fallback it would failover to a pre-approved region and we'd log it. If you denied fallback, requests will be queued or rate-limited. You can couple a surge policy to pre-warm spare Dedicated capacity.
[10:35] Priya: For DSARs, who handles deletion of cached artifacts — you or us?
[10:41] Elena: We assist: we can delete cache entries on request and provide confirmation. For long-term archival data in backups you should also run your retention/deletion policies. We'll document exact steps.
[10:54] Luis: About subprocessors — what is your onboarding questionnaire? Can we see the security attestation you require?
[11:01] Jordan: We'll include the subprocessor questionnaire template and the minimum attestation we require (SOC2 or ISO). We also perform an initial scoping assessment and periodic reviews.
[11:10] Priya: Any caveats around PII in prompts? We want to enforce prompt scrubbing for EU tenants at the edge.
[11:17] Elena: We can enable a prompt-sanitizer at the edge for EU tenants. That runs before hitting model inference and strips or tokenizes PII. This is configurable and can be tailored to your policies.
[11:30] Marcus: Final quick question: if a subprocessor changes their data center location, how is that surfaced?
[11:36] Jordan: Material changes show up in the change log and we do 30-day notices. For urgent security changes we notify immediately through our escalation contacts.
[11:45] Priya: Great. I think we have what we need for now. Next steps — send the attachments and schedule pilot.
[11:51] Jordan: We'll do that. Thanks everyone.
